result.question: What does Tesla disclose about its dependence on Elon Musk?
result.answer:
Tesla discloses in its risk factors that it is "highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk, Technoking of Tesla and our Chief Executive Officer" [0001628280-25-003063:item-1a-p016] [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p016] [0001628280-24-002390:item-1a-p015]. The company warns that the loss of services of key employees, including in particular Mr. Musk, could disrupt operations or delay the development, introduction, and ramp of its products and services [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p016] [0001628280-24-002390:item-1a-p015]. Tesla further notes that none of its key employees, including Mr. Musk, is bound by an employment agreement for any specific term, and it may not be able to successfully attract and retain senior leadership necessary to grow its business [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p016] [0001628280-24-002390:item-1a-p015].

Regarding Mr. Musk's time commitment, Tesla states that although Mr. Musk spends significant time with Tesla and is highly active in its management, he does not devote his full time and attention to Tesla [0001628280-25-003063:item-1a-p016] [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p017] [0001628280-24-002390:item-1a-p016]. In the 2025 10-K filed January 30, 2025, Tesla discloses that Mr. Musk also currently holds management positions at Space Exploration Technologies Corp., X Corp., X.AI Corp., Neuralink Corp. and The Boring Company, and is involved in other ventures and with the Department of Government Efficiency [0001628280-25-003063:item-1a-p016]. In the 2024 10-K filed January 29, 2024, Tesla similarly discloses that Mr. Musk serves as Chief Executive Officer and Chief Technical Officer of Space Exploration Technologies Corp., Chairman and Chief Technical Officer of X Corp., and is involved in other emerging technology ventures [0001628280-24-002390:item-1a-p016]. In the 2026 10-K filed January 29, 2026, Tesla discloses that Mr. Musk also currently holds management positions at Space Exploration Technologies Corp., X.AI Holdings Corp. ("xAI"), Neuralink Corp. and The Boring Company, and is involved in other ventures [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p017].

Tesla also discloses risks related to Mr. Musk's personal financial arrangements. Certain banking institutions have made extensions of credit to Mr. Musk, a portion of which was used to purchase shares of Tesla common stock, and these loans are partially secured by pledges of Tesla common stock owned by Mr. Musk [0001628280-25-003063:item-1a-p034] [0001628280-24-002390:item-1a-p034]. If the price of Tesla's common stock were to decline substantially, Mr. Musk may be forced to sell shares to satisfy his loan obligations, which could cause the stock price to decline further [0001628280-25-003063:item-1a-p034] [0001628280-24-002390:item-1a-p034]. In the 2026 10-K, Tesla adds that Mr. Musk may also sell a portion of his shares to satisfy tax obligations relating to the 2018 CEO Performance Award [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p035]. The 2026 10-K also discusses the 2025 CEO Performance Award, noting that the product goals were designed to incentivize Elon Musk to devote time and energy to development of specific products and services, and that misalignment of consumer demand with these technologies could impair Tesla's ability to realize returns on related investments [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p034].
